newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Air cargo operators stunned by Schiphol noise ban.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo operators stunned by Schiphol noise ban.

text.p: Schiphol's air cargo community is stunned by the announcement that the Dutch government is to allow a night ban on noisier aircraft, as well as pushing for tougher measures at the main Dutch airport.

Hans Knuvers, spokesman for ATAN, the Dutch air transport association, (which represents the forwarders, handlers and truckers associations), said: "It is absolutely amazing. It is an unprecedented move."

From Tuesday, noisier aircraft such as the McDonnell Douglas DC-10 and the Boeing 747 in its 100,200, 300 and SP versions will not be able take off during the time from 2300 to 0600 hours local time (2100 to 0400 gmt).
Schiphol came up with the plan in an effort to cut-back on noise levels at the airport and it had to be approved by the Dutch government.
Unscheduled take-offs and landings will also be banned. And new night flights from Royal Air Maroc, Spanair and El Al will be disallowed.
But Dutch Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma, said today these measures do not go far enough and that Schiphol should reconsider its position by September 1.
If the new plan to combat noise levels was not tough enough, she would consider sanctions that could mean closing all or part of the airport, she stated.

Knuvers said he could not believe that the Dutch Minister would even consider the first move. He was incredulous that she would consider closing the airport. "As if there was not enough bad news already."
"There is absolutely no mention of the economic effects of this ban. It is simply amazing," he said. And he questioned what impact this would have on Netherlands Inc.
Earlier, El Al said it would consider moving to another airport if the measures went ahead and Liege would probably be the most likely airport.

A Martinair said the only comment the airline had was that Martinair drew some consolation from the minister having said that the Dutch national carriers would be considered as having a special position compared to the foreign carriers.
